SEC22A-01.convention: germinate is standardly transitive, so the plural passive 'are germinated' is grammatical; only meaning ('sprout on their own') disfavours it, and a passive needs no human agent (germinated by warmth)
SEC22A-01.note: 'as well as' does not compound the subject; head is 'wild oat seeds' (plural), present habitual. B attracts via adjacent 'bindweed'; the voice axis is decided by meaning, not convention.

SEC22A-02.note: 'A number of' takes a plural verb; present results ('emit', 'are no smaller') call for present perfect. C attracts students who treat 'a number' as singular; D is plural but past progressive clashes with the present outcome.

SEC22A-03.note: 'hydroponics' (field/practice noun in -ics) is singular; passage is present tense. B attracts on the plural-looking form; C is singular but past.

SEC22A-04.note: Head 'a spheroid' is singular past the absolute phrase with plural 'cells'. Progressive is required because the growth is ongoing when the drug is added and then halts; D (simple present) would make the drug trigger proliferation, which is the strongest distractor and is decided by meaning.

SEC22A-05.note: Inside the relative clause the subject is 'the bird' (singular) and 'that' is the object gap, so the verb is active singular. B/C attract by agreeing with 'fig seeds'; A is singular but passive, impossible with an object gap.

SEC22A-06.note: Head 'units' is plural and receives the action (units are screened), so plural passive. D attracts via 'donor'/'antibody'; C is plural but active, making the units the screeners.

SEC22A-07.note: In the fronted comparative clause the subject is 'a single plant' and 'bees' is the fronted object; parallel with present 'secrete' gives simple present singular. C attracts via 'bees'; D is singular but perfect, mismatching the general-truth correlative.

SEC22A-08.note: 'which' takes plural 'samplers'; ongoing present operation ('give', 'continue') calls for present perfect progressive. A is plural but past; B attracts on 'county's'.

SEC22B-01.note: Head 'piezometers' is plural past the relative clause ending in 'technician ... boat'; past narrative ('filled', 'opened') requires past. B is plural but present; A attracts via 'technician'.

SEC22B-02.note: Plural 'wires' plus the agent phrase 'by hydrogen' force a plural passive. C attracts via the singular 'coating' in the intervening clause; D is plural but active, leaving 'by hydrogen' unattached.

SEC22B-03.note: Head 'a slab' is singular across a long prepositional chain ending in plural 'trails'; the slab 'remains attached at its base', so the process is ongoing, ruling out the completed 'has detached' (B), the strongest distractor.

SEC22B-04.note: Head 'alignment' is singular; 'between X and Y' does not compound it. Past 'as ... advanced' requires simple past. D attracts on the two headings; A is singular but present perfect against a past frame.

SEC22B-05.note: After 'nor' the clause inverts with do-support: bare 'measure' requires 'does', and the inverted subject 'instrument' is singular. The parallel 'have never sampled' tempts B/D, which fail because have/has cannot take a bare verb; C attracts via plural 'stations'.

SEC22B-06.note: 'The latter' refers to 'long wrought-iron rails' (plural); past narrative ('cracked', 'had replaced') needs simple past. B attracts students who read 'the latter' as singular; A is plural but present perfect.

SEC22B-07.note: Head 'one such icy moon' is singular past the parenthetical 'spacecraft measurements suggest'; 'jets' is the object, so active. B attracts via 'measurements'; D is singular but passive, leaving 'jets' with no role.

SEC22B-08.note: Head 'attempts' is plural past 'by a single amateur astronomer'; the paper is finished and printed, so ongoing 'are being documented' (D) is wrong. C attracts via 'astronomer'.

SEC22C-01.note: Head 'questionnaire' is singular (the plural possessive 'statisticians'' is a determiner); 'from the season it was printed' to now calls for present perfect. A attracts via the possessive; D is singular but simple present against the time span.

SEC22C-02.note: Compound predicate with plural 'retired teachers'; the registries closed two winters ago, so contribution cannot be ongoing, ruling out C (have been contributing). B attracts via 'museum'/'diary'/'schoolmistress'.

SEC22C-03.note: Inside 'whose' clause the subject is 'scripts' (plural); the occupation is past ('wrote'), so past passive. B attracts via 'the playwright'; D is plural but present.

SEC22C-04.note: 'which' refers to the varnish removal (or the varnish), singular either way, not the adjacent 'owners'; the 'whenever' frame is present habitual. B attracts via 'owners'; A is singular but perfect.

SEC22C-05.note: 'that' refers to 'the boys', not the adjacent 'priest' (who wears his everyday cassock); the grandmothers fit the costumes onto them, so plural passive. C attracts via adjacency; D ('are dressing as') is plural but active and only meaning rules it out. The detached restrictive 'that' is awkward but SAT-acceptable.

SEC22C-06.note: Head 'script' is singular past the 'unlike those of ... dramas' phrase; 'in each of the seasons that followed its premiere' to now calls for present perfect progressive. C attracts via 'dramas'; B is singular but simple present progressive.

SEC22C-07.convention: circulate is standardly transitive, so 'was being circulated' (by gossips) is grammatical singular past; only the gloss 'spread by itself' disfavours it, and gossip passing it along is still people circulating it
SEC22C-07.note: Head 'the claim' is singular past the noun clause ending in 'monks ... charters'. Voice is the deciding axis and it is settled by meaning, not a convention; B/C attract via 'charters'.

SEC22C-08.note: Inverted sentence: the fronted participial phrase is the complement, the true subject 'initials' follows the verb, so plural; the scholarly disagreement is present. B attracts by treating the gerund phrase as subject; D is plural but past.

tells: Every one of the 24 items tests subject-verb agreement on a 2x2 grid (number x tense/voice/aspect), with two singular and two plural options. A test-taker learns after a few items that the task is always 'find the head noun', and the noun printed right before the blank is usually the wrong number (e.g. SEC22A-01 'bindweed', SEC22A-06 'antibody', SEC22B-01 'boat', SEC22B-03 'trails', SEC22C-01, SEC22C-04 'owners', SEC22C-05 'priest', SEC22C-06 'dramas', SEC22C-07 'charters'). 'Choose the number opposite the nearest noun' works on most items but fails on SEC22A-04, SEC22A-05, SEC22A-07, SEC22B-04, SEC22B-06, SEC22B-08, so it is a strong prior rather than a clean tell.
Key letters are balanced (6 each of A-D) and keys split 12 singular and 12 plural, so no positional or number tell.

Within each set the non-number axis is decided by context, and in SEC22A-01 and SEC22C-07 it is decided by meaning only (active vs passive of a transitive verb), which is not a Standard English convention.
near_duplicates: voice decided by an 'on its own / spread by itself' gloss
relative clause whose true subject or antecedent is not the adjacent noun
inverted sentence with subject after the verb
plural head needing a passive past a singular attractor
ongoing process forces progressive over completed or simple form
singular head plus a time span to the present forces present perfect
past 'as ... advanced/filled' frame with a long modifier on the head
verb inside a which/whose relative clause agreeing past an intervening noun
